question: Can the Commission outline whether European Union law requires a separation between the generation and supply arms of publicly and/or privately owned electricity companies respectively?

Is there a distinction in the application of such a requirement if these companies or their subsidiaries are exclusively involved in generation and supply or are involved in the distribution and/or transmission of electricity?
Can the Commission specify the specific provisions in the relevant legislation?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.5.2024) EU law does not require a separation between undertakings generating (also called producing) electricity and undertakings selling (also called supplying) electricity to customers.

Nonetheless, Article 43 of Directive (EU) 2019/9441 requires ownership unbundling, meaning a structural separation between transmission system operators for electricity and undertakings involved in energy production or supply: a person or persons directly or indirectly controlling a transmission system operator are not entitled to directly or indirectly control or exercise any right over an undertaking performing any of the functions of energy production or supply and vice versa.

In case of public ownership two separate public bodies exercising control or rights are considered separate persons. Member States can apply alternative unbundling options in case of transmission systems that belonged to a vertically integrated undertaking as of 3 September 2009. The Commission has outlined its practice in assessing those unbundling requirements in Staff Working Documents and notes2.

Article 35 of Directive (EU) 2019/944 requires that distribution system operators for electricity are independent at least in terms of their legal form, organisation and decisionmaking from other activities not relating to distribution. Member States may decide not to apply those requirements to integrated electricity undertakings serving less than 100 000 connected customers or small isolated systems.
